rule: Setup-failure tests must assert the exception whose retry semantics match the intent: ConfigEntryNotReady when setup should be retried, ConfigEntryError when the failure is fatal.
trigger: A test named or documented as "not ready" asserts ConfigEntryError (or vice versa) around async_setup_entry.
rationale: The two exceptions mean different things to the config entry machinery - one schedules a retry, the other marks the entry failed - so asserting the wrong one hides which behavior the integration actually has.

evidence.excerpt: test name/docstring says "not ready", but the assertion expects ConfigEntryError

rule: Tests must reference the integration's own constants for config entry data and option keys instead of repeating raw string literals.
trigger: A test passes a bare string key into options={...} or data={...} of a config entry where the integration's const.py defines a constant for it.
rationale: Raw strings let the test keep passing after the integration renames the option, silently losing coverage.

evidence.excerpt: Use the integration constant for the option key (instead of the raw string)

rule: Service-call tests must pass values that are valid under the service schema (the integration's direction/mode constants), not stand-in primitives.
trigger: A test invokes an integration service or helper with integers/placeholders where the service schema expects domain constants such as DIR_LEFT/DIR_UP.
rationale: Schema-invalid values exercise a code path production calls never reach, so the test proves nothing about the real service.

evidence.excerpt: Use real pan/tilt direction values ... so the test matches the service schema

rule: Bluetooth integration tests must drive the integration through the public injection helpers (e.g. inject_bluetooth_service_info) rather than calling a coordinator's private _async_handle_bluetooth_event.
trigger: A test calls coordinator._async_handle_bluetooth_event(...) or another underscore-prefixed coordinator callback to simulate an advertisement.
rationale: Only the injection helpers run the same dispatch path as real passive scanning; calling the private callback skips the plumbing under test.

evidence.excerpt: Use the public Bluetooth test helpers instead of calling the coordinator's protected _async_handle_bluetooth_event

rule: Do not re-serialize existing JSON test fixtures; leave non-ASCII text as literal UTF-8 rather than \u escapes.
trigger: A diff in tests/components/*/fixtures/*.json rewrites accented characters as \uXXXX escapes or otherwise reformats untouched fixture lines.
rationale: Re-encoding produces churn unrelated to the change and makes the recorded device payloads harder to read against the vendor API.

evidence.excerpt: Revert the Unicode-escaped label ... to avoid unnecessary fixture churn

rule: Tests must not assert known-incorrect integration behavior as the expected value; leave the assertion out or mark it xfail until the integration is fixed.
trigger: A parametrized test case is accompanied by a comment calling the expected value a known bug or a follow-up fix.
rationale: Baking the bug into the suite means the eventual fix has to change tests that appear to be protecting correct behavior.

evidence.excerpt: This bakes a known incorrect behavior into the test suite

rule: Patch third-party helpers at the integration's import site (homeassistant.components.<domain>.<name>) rather than patching the library or stdlib module globally.
trigger: A test calls patch("shutil.which", ...) or patch("<library>.<func>", ...) for a symbol the integration imported into its own module namespace.
rationale: Patching the global module can miss the reference the integration actually resolves and leaks the patch across unrelated code.

evidence.excerpt: patch("homeassistant.components.picotts.shutil.which", return_value="/usr/local/bin/pico2wave")

rule: Do not add test fixtures - JSON fixture files, conftest fixtures, or fixture parameters in a test signature - that no test actually consumes.
trigger: A PR adds a file under tests/components/*/fixtures/, a fixture in conftest.py, or a parameter such as snapshot to a test signature that is never referenced.
rationale: Unused fixtures are dead test infrastructure; in a dependency-bump PR they also fall outside the stated scope and verify nothing.

evidence.excerpt: No test or fixture loader references anna_v4 ... falls outside the stated dependency-upgrade scope
fixture defined in conftest.py is not used by any test ... dead code
remove the unused snapshot fixture parameter

rule: Give each entity a translation_key so its name (and therefore its entity_id suffix) is distinct from the device name instead of the entity_id collapsing to button.<device>.
trigger: A new entity snapshot shows original_name/object_id_base as None and an entity_id equal to the bare device or container slug.
rationale: Without a translated entity name the entity is indistinguishable from the device and collides with sibling entities on the same device.

evidence.excerpt: Ensure the recreate button gets a distinct translated name ... rather than inheriting only the container name

rule: Tests that expect a translated HomeAssistantError must assert translation_domain and translation_key on the raised exception, not merely that some HomeAssistantError was raised.
trigger: pytest.raises(HomeAssistantError) around a service call in a test that parametrizes a translation_key without asserting it.
rationale: Bare pytest.raises passes for any failure, so the user-facing translated message the PR added is never actually verified.

evidence.excerpt: parametrizes translation_key but never asserts it ... only checks that some HomeAssistantError is raised

rule: Every translation_key introduced by an entity must have a matching entry added to the integration's strings.json in the same PR.
trigger: A new entity description or renamed entity appears in code/snapshots without a corresponding key under entity in strings.json.
rationale: Entity names are translated from strings.json; a missing key leaves the entity unnamed for every language.

evidence.excerpt: I think you still need to add it to the strings.json

rule: Entity-platform tests must assert the exact expected entity count (or snapshot the entities), never a loose lower bound.
trigger: assert len(states) >= N in a platform test, especially where a nearby comment claims a precise entity count.
rationale: A >= assertion cannot detect entities that silently stopped being created, and the comment and the bound drift apart.

evidence.excerpt: comment says "20 regular + 1 status = 21" but the assertion uses >= 10

rule: Media source tests must construct MediaSourceItem with the integration's own DOMAIN and a bare item identifier, not another integration's domain or a full media-source:// URI.
trigger: MediaSourceItem(hass, "<other-domain>", f"{media_source.URI_SCHEME}{DOMAIN}", ...) in a media source test.
rationale: Copy-paste values from another integration's tests still pass while describing the wrong item, misleading the next reader.

evidence.excerpt: copy-paste artifact from the immich tests ... should use DOMAIN and an empty identifier

rule: Recorder platform unit-conversion maps must be string-to-string; do not use None keys or empty-string units in the mapping.
trigger: A recorder platform test or implementation supplies a unit map entry like {None: ""} where the annotation is dict[str, dict[str, str]].
rationale: The documented contract maps one unit string onto another; a None key contradicts the annotation and relies on undefined behavior.

evidence.excerpt: uses {None: ""} as a unit mapping ... contradicts the return type annotation

rule: Syrupy snapshot names must be regenerated from the actual parametrization ids rather than hand-written, so they match the parameter values exactly.
trigger: A hand-edited .ambr entry whose bracketed id (e.g. [megane_e-tech]) differs from the parametrize source values (megane_e_tech).
rationale: A mismatched name makes Syrupy report the snapshot as missing and unexpected, failing the suite.

evidence.excerpt: Syrupy will treat these as missing/unexpected snapshots and fail

rule: Tests must not mutate a shared module-level CONFIG dict; copy it and set options on the nested integration config the integration actually reads.
trigger: A test assigns into a module-level CONFIG constant (config[CONF_X] = ...) rather than building a local copy of the nested domain config.
rationale: The mutation leaks into every other test in the module, and the top-level key is not where the integration reads the setting.

evidence.excerpt: Set the reconnect interval on the nested rflink config (and avoid mutating the shared CONFIG dict)

rule: A test's name and docstring must describe exactly the behavior it asserts; when they disagree with the assertions or with the PR's stated behavior, one of them is wrong and must be corrected before merge.
trigger: A test docstring describes a different outcome, service, or exception than the assertions in its body (including copied docstrings from a neighboring test).
rationale: Home Assistant requires a docstring on every test, so a stale one actively misleads reviewers about which behavior is protected.

evidence.excerpt: align the test expectations/docstring with the intended behavior
